# hear

> hear is a free Claude Code skill that lets Claude listen to audio and video files. It turns a file into a text report Claude can read (who spoke, what they said, and how they said it) plus a spectrogram image. Everything runs locally on macOS, Windows and Linux; audio never leaves the machine.

Claude has no audio input. hear works around that by running five local stages (Whisper first, the lighter four together) and writing their results as compact text:

- Transcript: every word with start, end and confidence (Whisper large-v3 turbo; MLX on Apple Silicon, faster-whisper elsewhere).
- Speakers: S1, S2… per line from a voice fingerprint (WeSpeaker ResNet34), with each speaker's share of talking time.
- Delivery marks: **louder**, (quieter), pitch ↑ ↓ relative to the speaker, line ends rising ↗ or falling ↘, pauses ‖0.8s‖, pace in words per minute, [?] for unsure words.
- Emotion: a tone guess per line when confident (emotion2vec+).
- Sounds: music, laughter, applause, whooshes and more, in 2-second windows every second (CLAP, zero-shot).
- Spectrogram: an image of the sound for anything the labels miss.

## Install

- macOS / Linux: `git clone https://github.com/kolinabir/claude-hear.git ~/.claude-hear && ~/.claude-hear/install.sh --warm`
- Windows (PowerShell): `git clone https://github.com/kolinabir/claude-hear.git $HOME\.claude-hear` then `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude-hear\install.ps1 -Warm`
- The skill lands in `~/.claude/skills/hear`. Then ask Claude Code, e.g. "listen to ~/Downloads/interview.mp4", or type `/hear <file>`.

## Facts

- Peak RAM: about 2.4 GB (Whisper runs first on its own; the lighter stages then run together).
- Disk: about 2.5 GB of models plus 2–3 GB of Python packages.
- Speed: a 40-second clip takes about 45 s on an Apple M4 (about 30 s with `--fast`). Without Apple Silicon or an NVIDIA GPU, transcription takes roughly the clip's length or more.
- Formats: anything ffmpeg reads (mp3, wav, m4a, aac, flac, ogg, mp4, mov, mkv, webm).
- Price: free. No API keys.

## Limits

- Delivery marks are cues, not proof of feelings.
- Emotion leans neutral; sound labels can confuse neighbours like laughing and coughing.
- Speaker labels are least reliable on very short lines and over loud music.
